assumptions.obligation: If i_rst_n_mst is asserted (falls, seen at i_clk_mst), i_rst_n_slv must also be asserted. Asserting the mst reset alone is not supported.
If i_rst_n_slv is asserted (falls, seen at i_clk_slv), i_rst_n_mst must also be asserted. Asserting the slv reset alone is not supported.
The requester keeps i_apb_psel low while either reset is asserted, so no transfer starts before both resets are released.
After the one-cycle Setup phase (PSEL=1, PENABLE=0), the requester keeps PSEL and PENABLE high (Access) up to and including the o_apb_pready cycle. No new Setup phase may come before PREADY.
APB5 only: if i_apb_pwakeup is high in a cycle where i_apb_psel is high, it must stay high until o_apb_pready is asserted.

notes:
Things I deliberately did not assume, because each would hide a real bug:
(1) Requester fields staying stable from Setup through Access (AB2-6.3-06). The spec defines what the bridge does when they change: it uses the Setup values and doesn't detect the change (AB2-6.3-25, AB2-12-06), and the regression plan includes a requester that changes fields (AB2-15.1-03). So changing fields stay legal, and the bridge's use of the Setup values remains checkable.
(2) PSTRB being low on a read (AB2-6.3-11). The bridge is specified to forward PSTRB as received (AB2-3-19, AB2-6.3-12).
(3) PENABLE high without a Setup cycle, or PENABLE without PSEL. The bridge must ignore these (AB2-6.3-24).
(4) Any completer-side input: i_apb_pready, prdata, pslverr, pruser, pbuser. Wait states without limit, errors and any data values are legal (AB2-3-10, AB2-6.3-26), and those signals only matter in the PREADY cycle.
(5) PWAKEUP being raised before PSEL. AB2-6.3-14 allows it before, during or after, AB2-6.3-15 is only a 'should', and AB2-15.1-03 uses a requester that never drives PWAKEUP. ENV-05 only requires it to stay high once it is high together with PSEL. It does not require it to stay high in the PREADY cycle itself, which is the weaker reading.

Not expressible with posedge-clocked immediate assumptions:
- PWAKEUP being glitch-free.
- Each reset being released synchronously to its own clock (AB2-3-39). This would need $global_clock.
- i_clk_slv being kept running while a request is in flight (AB2-20.2-02).
These must hold in the formal clock/reset setup or be checked in review.

ENV-01 and ENV-02 approximate 'asserted together' per domain: the other reset must be low at the first edge of the domain that sees its own reset fall. With very different clock speeds, this excludes a legal case: the other domain has already released its reset synchronously before that edge. Releasing one reset while the other domain is still in reset is not constrained (AB2-7.2-11).

ENV-04 and ENV-05 are gated on both resets being released. That keeps them from conflicting with ENV-03 during staggered release.
